prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (alias Ironwood): auto start by demand/depth; permissives suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips; lost permissive -> alarm/stop; maintenance release only after isolations tagged, verified, logged. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner; high-high level needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (alias Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket to Laboratory Technician; uses Jar Test Photograph Set to confirm dose in rapid raw-water change; adjusts only within approved limits, no auto substitute for operator review; shall hold last operator-approved dose if quality indications inconsistent/unavailable. North Filter Gallery (alias Cobalt): rapid headloss after verified chemical change -> may stagger washes. South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note to Chief Operator (shortened run/headloss/turbidity follow-up before next wash); breakthrough/delayed ripening -> out of production until Chief Operator approves. Washed filter returns only after rinse-to-waste meets target. Backwash Recovery Tank: recovery starts after filter backwash when turbidity/valve/flow confirmed; receives spent washwater; returns water only after settling and operator clarity check; out-of-band -> Chief Operator holds return, settle-and-decant. Chlorine Contact Basin: produces Chlorine Residual Alarm; maintains contact time. Clearwell Level Controller: sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit after verification; low-level interlock stops pumps; high-level alarm. High Service Pump Header (alias Juniper): sequences pumps, rotates lead/lag, paced pressure control; produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; on trip evaluates remaining pumps; supports North/South Distribution Pressure Stations. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (alias Sparrow): sends Jar Test Photograph Set. SCADA Historian Server (alias Lantern): stores audit, residual/level/pressure/pump data, recovery volume/tank level/turbidity/return timing. Actors: Chief Operator; Duty Engineer (reviews abnormal trends incl. repeated wash recovery); Maintenance Planner (alias Quarry); Laboratory Technician (sends Sample Chain Slip; storm priority turbidity/color/alkalinity/residual; results compared to online before sustained change); Distribution Dispatcher (alias Falcon); Chemical Supplier Driver (sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log); Residuals Hauler. Modes: Automatic; Manual; Reduced-capacity; Storm Intake Mode (solids

New part:
S165: The Chief Operator classifies upsets as advisory, controlled, or critical based on finished water risk, remaining treatment capacity, alarm persistence, and distribution service impact.
S166: An advisory upset requires closer monitoring and documented operator awareness but does not require immediate removal of treatment capacity.
S167: A controlled upset requires an operator-directed change, such as reducing filter loading, extending filter-to-waste operation, increasing verification sampling, or holding recovered washwater.
S168: A critical upset requires immediate protection of treated water quality, and the Duty Engineer is notified when automatic control cannot maintain the required operating envelope.
S169: A Chlorine Residual Alarm during a filtration upset is treated as a finished water protection issue rather than as an isolated chemical feed condition.
S170: The Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller are monitored together so that residual contact time, storage stability, and downstream pumping demand remain aligned.
S171: The High Service Pump Header is operated to maintain stable delivery while avoiding unnecessary pressure swings during recovery from a major wash or storm response action.
S172: The Distribution Dispatcher is notified when treatment changes could affect operating reserves at the North Distribution Pressure Station or South Distribution Pressure Station.
S173: The Chief Operator produces the Backwash Solids Manifest after solids removal quantities and handling conditions have been verified for the completed residuals event.
S174: The Maintenance Planner is informed when repeated solids handling problems indicate a need for inspection of tank mixing, decant valves, sludge transfer equipment, or instrumentation.
S175: Normal operation resumes when recovered water quality is stable, residuals handling is complete, alarms have cleared, and the Chief Operator confirms that the upset classification can be closed.
S176: Distribution monitoring begins at the High Service Pump Header, where discharge pressure, total flow, and pump status provide the control room with the first indication of system demand changes.
S177: The Distribution Dispatcher watches each pressure zone for sustained deviations rather than reacting to every short pressure fluctuation caused by hydrant use, valve movement, or customer demand changes.
S178: Normal control-room practice is to compare pressure trends with reservoir level trends, pump starts, and recent field activity before changing a setpoint.
S179: The North Distribution Pressure Station is monitored as a separate zone asset with its own suction pressure, discharge pressure, pump availability, and communication status.
S180: The South Distribution Pressure Station starts its lead booster pump when discharge pressure remains below the configured start band for the required delay period.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
